subject: Recap: Demo + Proposed 5-week POC Plan for Helios Logistics
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Isabel Cortez <icortez@helioslogistics.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@helioslogistics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:15:00 -0400
Subject: Recap: Demo + Proposed 5-week POC Plan for Helios Logistics

Hi Isabel / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through how Helios is thinking about automating freight docs and routing decisions. Quick recap from our side plus a proposed POC plan so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners. I attached a one-page PoC outline (Redwood_PoC_Outline_v1.pdf) and a draft SOW we can use to formalize scope.

High-level demo recap
- Showed prototype integration with Helios manifest CSV and routing API.
- Demonstrated 2 models: fast-generate routing suggestions (low-latency) and batch re-ranking for nightly route optimization.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns & token-level cost estimates in the Console.

Proposed 5-week POC (goal: validate production performance + business impact)
1) Week 0 (Prep, 1 week): access, sample dataset (anonymized), security checklist. Owner: Helios (Isabel) + Redwood infra lead (Marcus).
2) Week 1–2 (Integration): ingest sample feeds, wire routing API, run baseline tests. Owner: Soojin / Marcus.
3) Week 3 (Quality & Metrics): run evaluation prompts, define success metrics (accuracy on reranking >= 85% against historical decisions; average inference latency <= 250ms at 95th percentile). Owner: Rachel.
4) Week 4 (Load & Cost): scale tests to representative throughput; measure cost per 1k decisions and caching benefits. Owner: Marcus.
5) Week 5 (Review & Next Steps): executive demo, handoff plan + SOW negotiation.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm/adjust)
- Functional: Suggested routes match or improve existing heuristics on coverage/eta for 80% of sampled manifests.
- Performance: 95th percentile inference latency <= 250ms for the low-latency model.
- Economic: projected unit cost reduction >= 15% with batching + KV cache enabled.
- Integration: production-like API integration with Helios staging environment.

Action items / requests for Helios
- Share anonymized sample dataset (CSV) and API staging endpoint by EOD Friday.
- Confirm whether PII/data needs to remain in your VPC (Helios-managed) or can be processed on Redwood Hosted.
- Point security contact for SOC2 checklist review.

Proposed kickoff: Tuesday, June 16 — 30 minute kickoff to assign infra access and timelines. If VPC/private deployment required, we may need an extra week for networking.

Next steps from our side
- Marcus and I will prepare an infra checklist and PoC runbook (attached).
- Rachel will prepare the evaluation prompts and metric dashboard template.

Thanks — look forward to your thoughts.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: Redwood_PoC_Outline_v1.pdf (1 page), Redwood_SOW_template.docx (draft)

From: Isabel Cortez <icortez@helioslogistics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@helioslogistics.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Demo + Proposed 5-week POC Plan for Helios Logistics

Thanks, Soojin — good recap and thanks for the fast follow-up. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Security/VPC: We plan to require processing within our VPC for the POC (we'll have our security team review the SOC2 checklist). That may add some setup time — how long do you estimate for a Redwood Private VPC deployment?
2) Dataset: We can get an anonymized sample CSV ready by Friday. Expect ~3k rows (historical manifests) and a separate file for routing decisions.
3) Success metrics: The 85% threshold sounds reasonable, but can you provide a suggested evaluation prompt set and a short plan for how you measure "coverage" vs our heuristics?

Also looping Tom for budget & procurement questions — Tom, can we keep the weekly cadence but confirm whether we need an MSA or can proceed on the SOW?

Isabel
VP Product | Helios Logistics
icortez@helioslogistics.com

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 2:15 PM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Isabel / Tom —
> 
> Thanks again for taking time today to walk through how Helios is thinking about automating freight docs and routing decisions....

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Isabel Cortez <icortez@helioslogistics.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@helioslogistics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Demo + Proposed 5-week POC Plan for Helios Logistics

Isabel — thanks for the quick reply and the notes. Short answers up top, details below.

- VPC/private: We can run the POC inside Helios' VPC using our Redwood Private appliance. Typical network/setup time is 5–8 business days assuming your network team can open the required egress and we coordinate a short VPN. If you need an on-prem air-gapped install that will take longer.
- Evaluation prompts & coverage: Rachel has drafted an initial prompt set and an automated scoring script that compares model suggestions to historical routing decisions and computes coverage (fraction of cases where model suggestion matched or improved ETA/ETA variance). I'll attach the evaluation plan and sample prompts.

Updated timeline if VPC required
- Week 0 (Provisioning): 5–8 business days to stand up Redwood Private in your VPC. Owner: Marcus + Helios infra.
- Remaining weeks shift accordingly (we'll move integration to Week 1–2 after provisioning completes).

Security items we'll need from Helios
- Staging VPC CIDR and VPN details
- SSH key + temporary ingress for initial deploy (VPN preferred)
- ACLs for staging endpoints and S3 location for sample data
- Point security reviewer and preferred contact email

Attachments (included)
- Redwood_PoC_Outline_v1.pdf — updated with VPC notes
- Redwood_SOW_template.docx — draft for review
- Evaluation_Prompts_and_Scoring.txt — sample prompts and scoring logic

Proposed kickoff (revised): Monday, June 22 (allows a week for your security to review and for us to coordinate provisioning). If you prefer to start earlier and accept Hosted for the initial run, we can still begin June 16.

Next actions
- Isabel: confirm preferred deployment mode (Hosted vs VPC) and security contact.
- Tom: confirm procurement path (MSA + SOW vs PO + SOW).
- Marcus & Rachel (Redwood): we will prepare infra checklist and evaluation prompt set by Monday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with your security team if helpful.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_PoC_Outline_v1.pdf (updated), Redwood_SOW_template.docx, Evaluation_Prompts_and_Scoring.txt

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@helioslogistics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabel Cortez <icortez@helioslogistics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Demo + Proposed 5-week POC Plan for Helios Logistics

Thanks team — this looks good. Isabel: I'll get our procurement and security folks to review the SOW this week. We prefer MSA + SOW but can be flexible if timing is tight.

For provisioning: Isabel, can you share the security contact so Marcus can coordinate the VPN details? Also, can Redwood provide a short checklist of exact ports/egress we need to open for staging? That will speed things up.

Let's tentatively lock the kickoff for Monday, June 22 (pending SOW sign-off). If Helios wants to start earlier on Hosted, we are open to the June 16 date with the understanding we'll migrate to VPC later.

Tom Reed
Head of Procurement | Helios Logistics
tr@helioslogistics.com
